statement: An isolate is a manifest plus a code bundle, running in a worker, supervised, with the topics it's granted. Visual and headless code are the same kind of isolate.

events.why: Much of what's worth isolating draws nothing: state managers, sync engines, calculators. RFC 0001's "pane" made them fake an empty pane.

statement: The host starts and controls isolates with `kernel.spawn(manifest)`, `kernel.stop(id)`, `kernel.restart(id)` and `kernel.isolates()`. An isolate module exports `defineIsolate({ start(ctx) { … } })`, or an adapter's `defineIsolate(Component)`, and runs on `@isoloop/runtime`.

events.why: The names follow from the isolate being the unit.

statement: Each isolate runs in its own dedicated module worker unless its manifest names a pool.

events.why: Thread isolation is the main promise: a blocked or crashed isolate affects only itself.
The supervisor wired to real workers, built in M1.

statement: Placement is set in the host's manifest alone. Isolate code is the same in its own worker and in a pool, and an isolate module can't ask for a pool or refuse one.

events.why: Moving an isolate between placements is a config change, and the host decides what shares a worker.

statement: Nothing in the public API exposes which worker an isolate runs in. The supervisor, the compositor and the bus key everything by isolate id.

events.why: So pools could come later without breaking the API.

statement: `surface` is an optional manifest field: the host element an isolate renders into. An isolate without one is headless.

events.why: Headless isolates are first-class, not visual ones with an empty pane.

statement: A headless isolate starts with `renderFmt: 'none'`: no DOM subset is installed and `ctx.root` is `undefined`. It never reaches the compositor, and a `patch` it posts is dropped and counted.

events.why: A smaller, faster start for code that draws nothing.

statement: In a headless isolate, the host calls `measure`, `focus`, `scrollIntoView` and `requestCanvas` reject with `no_surface`. `navigate` still works.

events.why: There's no element to measure, focus or draw on.
The host calls `measure`, `focus` and `scrollIntoView`, built in M1.
`requestCanvas` shipped in M3a, so only headless isolates reject it.
events.prev: `measure`, `focus` and `scrollIntoView` reject with `no_surface` in a headless isolate, and `requestCanvas` rejects with `unsupported` in every isolate.

statement: A headless isolate gets the same supervision, heartbeats, bus access and replay as a visual one. When it crashes there's no fallback UI; the host sees `isolate:crash` and `isolate:failed`.

events.why: Headless code gets every guarantee visual code does.

statement: The unit isn't a pane with a `headless: true` flag.

events.why: Why not keep RFC 0001's pane and add a flag? The word would mislead for half the use cases.

statement: Isolates aren't actors: there's no mailbox per isolate and no addressing by isolate id.

events.why: Why not the actor model, which fits the supervision? Actor semantics, a mailbox per actor and addressing by id, are what the topic-based bus deliberately avoids.

statement: `manifest.suspend` is `'never'`, `'when-idle'` or `{ whenIdle: { afterMs } }`. `'never'` means Isoloop never suspends the isolate, in a hidden tab or anywhere else; `'when-idle'` waits 60 s.

events.why: A worker per isolate costs memory, so an app can let idle isolates go; isolates that keep state in memory must opt in knowingly.

statement: An isolate is idle when it has no visible surface, nothing was delivered for `afterMs`, it holds no `ctx.keepAwake()`, and no host call or acknowledged-pending publish is in flight. Off-screen, `display: none` and hidden-tab surfaces count as not visible; headless isolates are never visible.

events.why: Suspending must never cut off work that's still going on.

statement: `ctx.keepAwake()` keeps an isolate from being suspended until its release function is called. A hold has no time limit; devtools lists each with its age and where it was taken, and with `KernelConfig.dev` the console warns once a hold passes 10 minutes.

events.why: An isolate in the middle of work it can't see from the bus needs a way to say so.

statement: Suspending an isolate runs its `shutdown` with the usual grace, detaches it from the bus keeping its offsets, then terminates the worker. A suspended member of a consumer group leaves the group, so the group rebalances.

events.why: Suspension rebuilds from the log, so the isolate gets a chance to commit and to publish what it wants kept.

statement: A suspended visual isolate wakes when its surface becomes visible. A suspended headless isolate wakes when a record arrives on a topic it subscribes to, or a request does while it's the last member of its group. Either wakes on `kernel.resume(id)`.

events.why: Each kind wakes when it has something to do.

statement: Wakes go through a queue that starts at most 4 workers at a time, visible surfaces first in on-screen order, then headless isolates. Until an isolate renders, its surface shows the frozen snapshot of its last frame.

events.why: Waking many isolates at once would stall the page they're waking for.

statement: A bus restart wakes every suspended headless isolate: they resubscribe, replay and suspend again once idle. Suspended visual isolates aren't woken and catch up when shown.

events.why: The new bus has no record of the subscriptions the suspended isolates were waiting on.

statement: On waking, an isolate resubscribes from its committed offsets and replays what it missed. A subscription that asked for `from: 'latest'` resumes from `committed`, so nothing published while it slept is skipped. Losses arrive as `deliver.gap` or `reset`, never silently.

events.why: Suspension rebuilds from the log, for memory and persistent topics alike.

statement: The kernel warns when a suspendable isolate subscribes to a `last-n` or `time` topic, within about a second of the subscribe.

events.why: Retention may drop records before a sleeping isolate reads them; the warning comes from the bus metrics.

statement: Isolates aren't suspended automatically, even when every subscription is durable.

events.why: Why not suspend on its own when nothing would be lost from the log? Restarts become hard to predict, and isolates with in-memory state would lose it silently.

statement: There's no snapshot API for a suspended isolate's state.

events.why: Why not save and restore state on suspend? It's a second source of state next to the log; an isolate publishes what it wants kept to a compacted topic on shutdown instead.

statement: A record doesn't wake suspended visual isolates.

events.why: Why not wake every suspended isolate on any record? It wakes hidden visual isolates for records nobody can see; they catch up from the log when shown.
